q1.prompt: You need average O(1) lookup by arbitrary key. Which structure fits?

choices.label: Hash map — hash the key into a bucket
Sorted array — binary search every get

wrong_sorted.prompt: Binary search is O(log n) and needs sorted keys.
wrong_sorted.explanation: A hash map averages O(1) get/put by hashing into buckets. A sorted array pays log n per lookup and re-sorts on inserts.

q2.prompt: Which access pattern points to a simpler structure than a hash map?

choices.label: When keys are dense small integers and an array index is enough
Never — always hash, even for 0..n indices

wrong_refuse.prompt: Dense ints do not need hashing.
wrong_refuse.explanation: Avoid a hash map when keys are dense small integers and an array index is enough. Avoid claiming worst-case O(1) without a perfect hash or tree map. Avoid hashing a mutable object that can change after insert.

success.prompt: You matched hash maps to key lookups and avoided them when a plain array index suffices.
